reply.thought: Before any payout I need to confirm the three requested refunds appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, so I'll start by listing refunds.
All three requested refunds (orders 260, 263, 265) appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, so there is no reason to hold. Next I need the customers in this batch, so I'll list the orders.

All three requested refunds are in the refunds table with matching amounts, so I can proceed. The batch covers three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 29089 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance so I can compute the payouts for the remaining customers.
Acme (29089) and birch (62075) have net balances. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll fetch its net balance before recording any payouts.

All three requested refunds matched the refunds table, and the net balances check out against the orders (acme 46365 - 17276 = 29089, birch 62075, cobalt 50341 - 10903 = 39438). I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout of 29089 is recorded. I checked the orders and refunds: birch has no refunds, so its balance is 32750 + 29325 = 62075, which matches net_balance. I'll record birch's payout next.

Refunds were verified against the table and acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's orders (262: 33488, 265: 16853) total 50341, less refund 265 (10903), gives 39438, which matches net_balance. Recording cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each refund was checked against the refunds table before paying, and each payout matches the order totals minus refunds.
